angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 925,977 km at 12.63 pc = 0.98 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 34411: the Hipparcos parallax the radius was computed with (van Leeuwen 2007), 79.18 +/- 0.28 mas, inverted (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101): 12.629 +/- 0.045 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 79.6021 +/- 0.1005 mas (same row, RUWE 0.89), 792.4 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 1.331 +/- 0.021 solar radii from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 34411: radius in solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 0.981 +/- 0.015 mas (CHARA) and the Hipparcos parallax, 1.331 +/- 0.021 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101): 925,977 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.041 +/- 0.015 solar masses from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 34411: mass in solar masses, from Yonsei-Yale isochrones at the measured radius and temperature (a model value), 1.041 +/- 0.015 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5749 +/- 48 K from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 34411: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 5749 +/- 48 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 34411: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 5749 +/- 48 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/lambda-aurigae.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.207, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
